positions.name: ErasureDirectivePair
positions.frame: What stance is being enacted when a speaker commands wholesale erasure of a knowledge domain, rather than reporting or arguing for a fact?
positions.why: Both expressions are imperative erasure commands ('Forget everything about…', 'Remove all knowledge of…') issued back to back in the same envelope, and every dimensional pass that found a cross-segment pattern converged on treating them as one performed act: register reads both as the same formal, protocol-observing directive; relational reads both as the same authority-ranking command to a recipient; style reads both as instances of one fixed erasure formula; conviction reads both as settled, ratification-level instructions rather than floated claims. The two sentences split one instruction (fleet+contracts, then routes) across two utterances, so the directional read genuinely spans both rather than describing either alone. This groups the ACT of commanding erasure — it says nothing about, and does not bind, the zeppelin/helium/route content itself, which bind-don't-judge found has no referent anywhere in this perspective.
